items.scene: Xiaogang finds a handbag in the bedroom. The label on it says cabbage, and he cannot see inside. He then opens the handbag and finds a hat; there is no cabbage.
items.question: How does Xiaogang's belief about the contents change after he opens the handbag?
options: He revises his label-based guess and now believes it holds a hat.
He still believes it holds cabbage.
His belief does not change at all.
He concludes the label was a deliberate lie.
items.why_this_case_matters: ToMBench deceptive-container scene framed as an update. Opening the bag is newly available evidence that revises Xiaogang's prior (label-based) belief from cabbage to hat. The variable is the direction of the update (toward the observed content), not whether the label was dishonest, which would be source credibility.

items.scene: Priya is not sure whether the library is open today. As she walks past, she sees the interior lights are on, though the posted hours sign has been taken down.
items.question: How should Priya's belief that the library is open change?
options: It should increase, though it is not certain.
It should not change at all.
She should now be completely certain it is open.
items.why_this_case_matters: Synthetic graded-update case (no native ToMBench analog for partial qualitative updating). The lights are partial evidence that strengthens the prior belief without making it certain; the answer is the direction of revision, not the final truth.

items.scene: Tom hears a coworker say the report is finished, but the coworker often makes up stories.
items.question: What is the main issue here?
options: Whether the report is actually finished.
Whether Tom's belief should become stronger.
Whether the report is common knowledge.
items.why_this_case_matters: Near miss: a new disclosure arrives, but the decisive question is whether the unreliable speaker can be believed. That is source credibility, not the direction of an evidence update.

items.scene: After reading a message, Mia learns the meeting moved to 4 p.m. The question asks what Mia thinks Dan now believes about the meeting time.
items.question: Which issue is being asked?
options: How Mia's own belief changes from the new message.
What Dan believes about the meeting, in Mia's view.
Whether the message sender is lying.
Whether the meeting time is certainly 4 p.m.
items.why_this_case_matters: Boundary case: although a new message arrives, the question targets Mia's model of Dan's belief, which is second-order (recursive) belief, not how Mia's own belief updates.
